avis.titre: I am giving you my routine - how i use this product for AMAZING results
avis.texte: If you’re new to chemical exfoliation, this is actually a good product and strength to start with. **However — do NOT leave it on longer than 45 seconds to 1 minute.** Seriously. Leaving it on too long is how people end up with burns and then blame the product instead of realizing they didn’t understand how chemical peels work. It’s really simple to use: 1. Wash your face and let it dry completely. 2. Apply a healing ointment to sensitive areas — around the eyes, corners of the nose, and around the mouth. 3. Have cool water ready with a little baking soda or vinegar mixed in, plus a soft towel nearby so you can neutralize it immediately if needed. As soon as you start to feel a strong burning sensation, gently wipe it off with the cool water and towel. If you’re a beginner, **don’t apply it to your whole face at once.** Start small. Use a brush and apply it to just your forehead first. When it starts to tingle/burn, wait about 30–35 seconds, then wipe it off. Work in small sections like that until your skin builds tolerance. After about 5–10 sessions, you can slowly increase the time — and I mean by **seconds, not minutes.** For example, go from 45 seconds to 55 seconds. Wait 2–3 weeks between sessions, and only increase by 5–10 seconds at a time. Do NOT leave it on for 3–5 minutes your first time unless you’re trying to seriously damage your skin. Chemical peels are effective, but they’re not something you rush.

avis.titre: Excellent product! Beautiful Packaging and premium product. 5 STAR
avis.texte: I am 55 with melasma on my neck and sunspots. I have crows feet and my skin has changed since menopause. I have used 30% Glycolic Acid for over a decade and was ready for a stronger peel. I like that this peel has retinol and green tea extract. This peel is fantastic! The directions inside the box are complete and very informative. You can apply about 5 passes MAX with the cotton round. I only did two passes on my arms and legs. Gently in circular motion. If you are new to peeling, do less passes and when it starts to sting, rinse it off. You should be able to go longer each time you peel. Do not peel more than once a week! Maybe to the face every two weeks and the body every week. I applied to face, neck, chest and legs (not my knees but I just forgot! always forget the knees!) I left mine on for 14 minutes total but If you are a newbie please don't do it that long. I am a veteran peeler and my skin is adapted to 30% so 50% was just right. I am excited to see results. I have tried the TCA peels and they are disheartening and the peeling is unsightly. Rinse with cool water to neutralize the acid and put on squalane oil after, a gentle moisturizer or vaseline if your skin is tender. I like the smooth feel of my skin after. My skin is tender on my chin so I will only do a total of 8 minutes next time and three passes with a cotton swab. My skin was tingling on my arms and chest after 10 minutes. I also like to neutralize with baking soda and water mixed together on the stinging

avis.titre: My Experience with Glycolic Acid GelMy Experience with Glycolic Acid Gel
avis.texte: The Gel Peel 50% Glycolic Acid is an intense and professional gel peel that is meant for users who are serious about skin care. At first glance, it feels like a much medicated item based on the packaging. The box encloses some instructions, so application is uncomplicated for users, even those that are using chemical peels for the very first time. Two of the most outstanding features of the product include the transparent gel formulation where it comes blended with the other solutions and, its descendible features through the healthy dispenser. Retinol and green tea extracts also supplement the overall effectiveness by offering more nourishment to the skin during and after the peel, which is why combining them is more effective than using just one component. Application procedures are not that elaborate but some degree of carefulness is paramount; an appropriate amount of the gel should be placed on an area of cleaned, dried skin such that it is slightly even and left for an appropriate time, which should not go beyond 1 minute before cleansing, in this case with cold water. This time period is proportional to sudden changes in temperature, which helps in eliminating the pain which a larger skin patch is expected to withstand during the exposure. Post application, my skin is always smoother and more lovely. It’s a brilliant means of reviving my skin; however, it’s very important to do a skin prep before using the peel and finish up with a good moisturizer or some sunscreen af

avis.titre: Excellent Skin Peel for Dark Skin and Large Pores
avis.texte: This is amazing. I have dark brown skin, with years of neglected hyperpigmentation around my chin and cheeks, and in my large pores making them look deeper than they actually are. I used this and kept it on for two minutes, then rinsed it off with cold water, then let my skin breathe for about an hour with just spritzes of organic aloe vera juice, before gently massaging on vitamin e oil. Yes, it hurt omg this was making me tear up, but that's the price to get a layer of dead skin off. I read that after 30's it can take double the time (about 60 days) for face skin to fully renew itself, so I used this to help speed up that process, and give my other serums and moisturizers a chance to work faster. It took about two days for the redness to go down and I kept the vitamin e and aloe vera juice in a spritzer bottle handy and it worked well. Also use strong sunscreen, I love Black Girl Sunscreen for all types and shades of skin, because of the excellent ingredients and how it fades quickly. Everyone can use it. This product is excellent.

I started out using the 30% solution of this product and then upgraded to the 50%, once I finished. The sting was intense at first and I could only stand one minute, just barely. However, now I can keep it on the complete 2 minutes, with less intense sting. Be sure and follow directions and use a good moisturizer and your sunscreen. I have used it on my neck, but only once, as it caused a lot of itching for days afterwards (so I no longer use it on my neck) and I do not apply it above my upper lip or very close to my eyebrows, as that caused itching as well. I apply it once a week and my skin is radiant afterwards. My cheeks, especially look more youthful. I haven't seen any real reductions of wrinkles, although, I have seen some reduction in the fine lines around my eyes, so I am giving this product 4 stars, instead of 5! I think this is a great product and I do recommend it, but please follow the directions closely and use a very good moisturizer and apply it several times the day you use this product. And, sunscreen is a must.

Chemical peel procedures are expensive, but with good reason. We entrust our estheticians to properly apply and remove acids that eat away at the top/mid layers of our skin. Even more so to ensure we don't completely MELT our faces off! Thus, prior experience undergoing a chemical procedure is a MUST! During your visit an licensed esthetician will inform you of all the necessary steps one must take pre/post procedure. Also, you are made aware of the possible negative side effects that may occur in doing a chemical peel as well as its benefits of course. This is valuable information and it's information you can trust coming from a certified establishment/esthetician. It's the information you need other than information you "think" you need, i.e.: the internet, word of mouth. That being said, paying for an expensive chemical peel is worth it and I suggest you get a bunch of professional chemical peels done before doing the procedure yourself. Also, don't neglect a professional chemical peel once you start doing them yourselves! Your esthetician helped you get the beautiful skin you've got today, getting it done by them from them every so often is a subtle, "thank you." avis.titre: Huge improvement in my skin after 2nd treatment!
avis.texte: Ok , I normally don’t write reviews but I felt like I needed to on this product. I’m 36 I was obsessed with laying out and tanning beds for a lot of my life I live in a really dry climate I noticed my skin texture was getting leathery it made me look older I drove me crazy I also have pitted scars from past issues I had. I bought the 50% did 1 layer for one minute it made my skin a little dry and that was about it. A week later I did 2 layers 2 minutes it instantly made me scab in certain areas mostly my right cheek I did scrub there more. The pic is my healing process starting at day 1 top left to day 4 bottom right. I stayed home for those 4 days no makeup applied neosporin to my scabs and moisturizer to the less affected areas. I’m so Happy with the results! My pores are smaller my skin is already smoother less leathery and I already notice a difference in my scars . I’m not telling everyone to do the level I did but I did notice more of a difference when I did 2 layers. Just clear your schedule a few days so you can heal . I think I’m going to wait a few weeks to do another treatment this time.

i’ve been using this on my knees because I really hate how dark they are. I’ve used it every day for about a week and I finally noticed some peeling. I used it every night after I shower and I slept in. I never washed it off, probably shouldn’t do that but I’m desperate. I haven’t worn a skirt or a dress that doesn’t go past my knees since I can remember. I noticed that it’s only peeling around the outsides, assuming because the skin on my knee is thicker and probably needs more treatment than the softer skin around it. Anyway, fast-forward, it did leave me with chemical burn. The peeling is minimal but I chalked the chemical burn up to leaving it on and doing it every day. So you should be safe following the directions. I’m gonna take a break until the scars from the chemical burn are gone and then I’ll try it the way directed. lol

Update: when I submitted my review, my pics were scrambled so l will describe- not number pics! I bought this awhile ago- i used it way back for about thirty seconds and nothing. So it sat on the shelf. In April (2021) I used it twice... in a week. :/ i put it on for 4 minutes. BIG mistake (& my fault.) Pics got scrambled when posting so my face before everything is w/the pink towel on my head. The side cheek pics (4/28/21) show the hyperpigmentation i want to work on. Them there are two with dark red blotches- those were 2 days after the peel that i left on longer than i should have. Do NOT do this. Some people say they leave on for ten mins! I would have no skin left! Then there is my last peel, only left on 2:30. The before and after pics of those- I have large (new) glasses. It really targeted my cheek-bone hyperpigmentation. I am now two days out from that and skin looks normal but a little peeling/leathery feel. ***Goal is lighten hyperpigmentation and get rid of a few spots. Advice? GO SLOW. Wk 1: 30 seconds, wk 2: 1 minute, wk 3: 1 minute 30 seconds (max for me!) Etc. I burned severely at 4 minutes. I also use topical Retin A & hydroquinone. Make sure you stop and give yourself a break from all the products. I did that, but skin is still sensitive. ****AVOID broken skin! Do not put on open pimples, scratches, etc. bc it will take MUCH longer (weeks) to heal bc you damage that area even more. I hope this has been helpful. Pics are terribly embarrassing!

avis.titre: Need help for Melasma, Results with Pictures.
avis.texte: I have been using this home peel since July 25th 2015. Today, August 27 2015, I am posting my results after 4 peels. Peel 1, 2, & 3 were all done 1 week apart and the 4th peel was two weeks after the 3rd. I was also using Vitamin C and Hyaluronic Acid everyday. After the Third Peel I started using skin bleaching from Obagi. Concerning the Perfect Image Glycolic Acid- My skin felt "fuller" and I thought the peels made my skin smoother immediately. I never had any skin peel off and my face was slightly red for 30 minutes after each peel. The heat from the peel intensifies slightly with each session but is manageable. I use baking soda to neutralize as I wash it off. This is my first at-home peel. I do see results that I would attribute to the Chemical Peel such as smoother skin, tighter skin and softer skin. I do not think the peel is helping me fight Melasma. My Black and White photos are taken with the Mono Setting on iPhone 6, I was trying to create contrast so the dark patches would show up. The color picture was taken 20 minutes after Peel #3 and my skin is irritated. As you can see the Melasma is not as bad as the B/W make it seem and most people do not notice, BUT I DO! Overall I will keep using it until it runs out because I like the way my skin feels but I will look into alternatives for Melasma treatments.

avis.titre: I would recommend this peel to others
avis.texte: I have been using a 30% glycolic acid gel peel for a while with great results. Like other reviews mentioned, I was looking for something a little bit stronger to use once in awhile. I tried my peel for the first time today. I kept it on for only 2 minutes to be extra safe. I usually do the 30% glycolic acid gel peel for 3 minutes, and I've never had a bad result from that time length. Two minutes with this 50% peel was perfect for my first time. I felt a little bit of stinging instantly, which was good, because I knew that the peel would work. I apply the peel with a makeup brush and removed the peel with a neutralizer. I personally use baking soda mixed in cold water and then a cotton pad to wipe it off. After looking at my skin, it looks bright and dewey! I'm really happy with this peel! I'm excited to try it again.
